note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers, synonymic citations and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very similar to A. ignavus, from which it differs in mandibular proportions and in the degree of constriction of the meso- and metanotum, but the two records are more than 1000 miles apart and no intermediate specimens are known. A. ivrixosus is closer in body size to the present species than to A. ignavus, with a more inflated postclypeus and shorter cephalic pilosity in the alate, and different mandibular proportions in the worker. A. empodius differs in the mandibles of both alate and worker, has shorter alate pilosity, and its worker enteric valve seat is quite different. The worker abdomen appears non-dehiscent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity yellow, long, abundant and conspicuous. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.30, Pcl/Rj 2.63; mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.64, Ra/Ri 0.85; a distinct notch, in surface view, separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence, L4/L1·Lm 7.90; the first marginal tooth of the right mandible lies slightly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, and its anterior margin is distinctly shorter than that of the second marginal tooth, Ra/Ri·Rm 10.46. Fore tibia slender, Ti/Tw 5.80; third apical spur reduced. The midgut–hindgut junction is oblique and meets the Malpighian tubule knot on the right side; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is lateral, weakly bilobed, and joined to the second hindgut pouch by a long neck; the valve membrane bears sparse minute spines outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule chestnut brown, darker above the ocelli; fontanelle elliptical, its outline ill defined, about half the ocellus, flat or slightly concave, concolorous with the head capsule; central spot circular, flat, slightly smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous; postclypeus chestnut brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal groove flat, a very indistinct crescent, concolorous with the head capsule; antennae brown. Pronotum chestnut brown, meso- and metanotum brown, transverse sutures weak or absent; femora and tibiae yellowish brown, tarsi pale yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles dark brown; sternites yellowish brown with a yellow median area, ventral spiracles brown; cerci pale brown. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli small, their distance from the compound eye slightly less to slightly more than their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.19–0.21, Pcl/Ra 2.33–2.53, posterior margin broadly rounded or slightly angular, median suture very weak. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.55–0.59, Ra/R4 0.83; a distinct notch, in surface view, separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 6.60–6.81; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are aligned, and the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is distinctly longer than that of the second. Cephalic pilosity brown, with a definite layer of short hairs beneath very long outstanding setae; the longest setae extend well beyond the outer margin of the compound eye. Meso- and metanotum narrower at the constriction, M/W 0.26–0.27. Third apical spur of the fore tibia distinct.
